Moon et al. conducted a multi-center study evaluating the Bio-Rad Genius HIV-1/2 confirmation assay as an alternative to the Western blot for the Korean population. Their findings, published in PloS One in 2015 (Volume 10, Article e0139169), highlight the assay's potential utility in clinical settings. 3. Pando and colleagues explored improved HIV diagnostic strategies for men who have sex with men (MSM) in Buenos Aires, Argentina, a population with high HIV prevalence and incidence. Their work, published in HIV Medicine in 2012 (Volume 13, Issue 9, Pages 564–567), underscores the importance of tailored approaches in high-risk groups. 4. Shima-Sano et al. developed an HIV screening algorithm to address the high rate of false-positive results in pregnant women in Japan. Their study, published in PloS One in 2010 (Volume 5, Issue 2, Article e9382), emphasizes the need for accurate diagnostic tools in this population. 5. Walensky et al. examined the expectations and outcomes of rapid HIV testing in emergency departments. Their findings, published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2008 (Volume 149, Issue 3, Pages 153–160), provide valuable insights into the implementation of rapid testing in acute care settings. 6. Keller, Jones, and Erbelding investigated the impact of rapid HIV testing choices on care entry in Baltimore City sexually transmitted infection clinics. Their study, published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2011 (Volume 25, Issue 4, Pages 237–243), highlights the role of testing in facilitating timely care. 7. Peruski, Dong, and Selik analyzed trends in HIV testing algorithms in the United States and six dependent areas from 2011 to 2015. Their research, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2018 (Volume 103, Pages 19–24), provides a comprehensive overview of diagnostic practices. 8. Stevinson et al. conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of the New Jersey rapid testing algorithm for HIV testing in publicly funded sites. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2011 (Volume 52, Supplement 1, Pages S29–S33), demonstrate the economic benefits of optimized testing strategies. 9. Obare et al. assessed the acceptance of repeat population-based voluntary counseling and testing for HIV in rural Malawi. Their study, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2009 (Volume 85, Issue 2, Pages 139–144), highlights the importance of community engagement in testing programs. 10. Nasrullah et al. evaluated the role of state public health laboratories in HIV testing. Their findings, published in Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 73, Issue 2, Pages 164–172), underscore the critical role of laboratory infrastructure in public health. 11. Delaney et al. demonstrated the use of a multitest algorithm to improve the positive predictive value of rapid HIV testing and linkage to care in nonclinical settings. Their study, published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016 (Volume 71, Issue 1, Pages 78–86), highlights the importance of robust diagnostic pathways. 12. Chen and Yao compared the turnaround time and total cost of HIV testing before and after implementing the 2014 CDC/APHL Laboratory Testing Algorithm. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2017 (Volume 93, Page 45), emphasize the efficiency of updated diagnostic protocols. 13. Cardenas, Baughan, and Hodinka evaluated the Bio-Rad Multispot HIV-1/HIV-2 Rapid Test as an alternative to Western blot confirmation. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2013 (Volume 58, Supplement 1, Pages e97–e103), highlights the test's potential in clinical diagnostics. 14. Goodhue et al. reported on the implementation of fourth-generation HIV screening in Massachusetts, showcasing a partnership between laboratory and programmatic efforts. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2013 (Volume 58, Supplement 1, Pages e13–e18), demonstrate the benefits of integrated approaches. 15. Hutchinson et al. analyzed the costs and outcomes of laboratory diagnostic algorithms for HIV detection. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2013 (Volume 58, Supplement 1, Pages e2–e7), provides insights into the economic and clinical implications of testing strategies. 16. Styer, Sullivan, and MP evaluated an alternative supplemental testing strategy for HIV diagnosis through retrospective analysis of clinical data. Their findings, published in Journal of Clinical Virology in 2011 (Volume 52, Supplement, Pages S35–S40), highlight the potential for improved diagnostic accuracy. 17. Clark et al. discussed the role of public health laboratories in supporting HIV testing services. Their work, published in Public Health Reports in 2008 (Supplement 3, Pages 86–93), emphasizes the importance of laboratory quality assurance. 18. Meulbroek et al. described the BCN Checkpoint initiative, which provides same-day confirmation of reactive HIV rapid tests using point-of-care HIV-RNA testing. Their study, published in HIV Medicine in 2018 (Volume 19, Supplement 1, Pages 63–65), highlights the benefits of accelerated linkage to care and reduced patient anxiety. 19. Ryan et al. evaluated and refined a community model of HIV testing in Australia through a trial-and-error approach. Their findings, published in BMC Health Services Research in 2017 (Volume 17, Article 692), underscore the importance of iterative program development. 20. The World Health Organization's 1997 revised recommendations for selecting and using HIV antibody tests provide a foundational framework for diagnostic practices. These guidelines are further consolidated in the 2019 guidelines on HIV testing services. 21. Sands et al. discussed the implications of serological false reactivity for HIV testing algorithms at the 2018 African Society for Laboratory Medicine conference in Abuja, Nigeria, emphasizing the need for accurate diagnostic tools. 22. Kosack et al. designed HIV testing algorithms based on the 2015 WHO guidelines using data from six sites in sub-Saharan Africa. Their study, published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2017 (Volume 55, Issue 10, Pages 3006–3015), highlights the importance of context-specific diagnostic strategies. 23. The UNAIDS 90-90-90 initiative, launched in 2015, sets ambitious treatment targets to help end the AIDS epidemic. These goals are integrated into the 2019 consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services. 24. Quality management systems are essential for all aspects of HIV testing services, including laboratory-based, health facility-based, and community-based testing. These systems ensure accurate, timely, and reliable diagnoses, which are critical for effective HIV care and treatment programs.
